channel.title: Use & Like: app news
channel.description: What changed in the apps you use, in our own words, with what it means for you and what to do about it.

item.title: Black Friday scams 2026: fake shops, delivery texts and fake numbers
item.description: The Black Friday scams warned about this month copy real shops, carriers and customer service lines, and going straight to the shop's own app or website and paying by credit card protects against most of them.

item.title: Passkeys vs passwords explained: how they work on iPhone and Android
item.description: A passkey lets you sign in with your face, fingerprint or phone PIN instead of a password, and because it never leaves your device as a secret you could type in, a fake website can't trick you into handing it over.

item.title: Phone overheating with CarPlay or Android Auto: why and what helps
item.description: A phone running CarPlay or Android Auto often does several heavy jobs at once (navigation, music, mobile data and charging) in a warm car, and Apple and Google both say long navigation sessions, sunlight and hot cars make phones heat up, so a cable, a shaded spot and a lighter load usually help.

item.title: Tromsø northern lights app made by local aurora guides
item.description: Guide To Tromsø is an iPhone and iPad app for the northern lights in Tromsø, Norway, made by local aurora guides: it shows live aurora data, a cloud map, recent sightings from other users and viewing spots. It costs 49 cents once, with no subscription, and was #96 among paid Travel apps on the US App Store on 19 November.

item.title: ChatGPT ads on Free and Go plans: what they look like and who sees them
item.description: ChatGPT shows ads to people on its Free plan and the $8-a-month Go plan, now in 89 countries, while Plus, Pro and Enterprise stay ad-free. An Android Police writer says the ads now show up after nearly every reply on Go.

item.title: Affiliate links on Instagram Reels and YouTube explained
item.description: An affiliate link pays the creator a commission when you buy through it, and since 16 November US creators can put Amazon affiliate links right into Instagram Reels and feed posts, as YouTube creators already can with tagged products.

item.title: AI Photo Edit: online AI photo editor that works from one sentence
item.description: AI Photo Edit is a web photo editor where you upload a picture, type the change you want, and it redraws only that part. It can swap outfits or backgrounds, remove people or text and restore old prints.

item.title: App Store Awards 2026 finalists: 45 apps and games picked by Apple
item.description: Apple named 45 finalists for its 2026 App Store Awards across iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, Vision Pro and Apple Arcade, plus a Cultural Impact group. The iPhone App of the Year finalists are ElevenReader, (Not Boring) Camera and Raylie.

item.title: Banking app security issues: half of 2,686 apps had serious flaws
item.description: Security firm Ostorlab tested 2,686 mobile banking apps from 487 banks in 64 countries and found that 51.5% had at least one high or critical security problem. Its scanner got past the fingerprint or face login in 35.1% of the Android apps.

item.title: Bitwarden passkey manager now works natively in Windows 11 and macOS
item.description: Bitwarden's desktop app can now be set as the passkey provider in Windows 11 and macOS, so the system's own passkey window saves and uses passkeys from your Bitwarden vault. It works in websites without the browser extension.

item.title: ChatGPT dictation time limit removed with new Live Dictation
item.description: ChatGPT's dictation now writes your words on screen while you're still speaking, and the old 10-minute recording limit is gone. OpenAI is rolling it out on all plans, free included, on iPhone, Android, the web and the desktop app.

item.title: Connecticut Mobile ID app: your driver's license on your phone
item.description: Connecticut's free Mobile ID app puts your driver's license, learner's permit or state ID on your phone from 18 November. The TSA accepts it at participating airport checkpoints, but police and polling places don't.

item.title: Daybreak exports Apple Health data to CSV and JSON files
item.description: Daybreak is a new $0.99 iPhone and iPad app that copies up to 80 daily Apple Health metrics into CSV and JSON files in a folder you pick. It was #80 among paid Health & Fitness apps on the US App Store on 18 November.

item.title: Flood Atlas: free South Florida flood map app with alerts and routes
item.description: Flood Atlas is a free iPhone app that puts National Weather Service flood alerts, NOAA tide and river gauges and neighbours' flooded-street reports for South Florida on one map. It was #39 among free Weather apps on the US App Store on 18 November.

item.title: Foldwriter typewriter app: a half-folded iPhone Duo types letters
item.description: Foldwriter is a $1.99 app that shows paper on the top half of a half-folded iPhone Duo and typewriter keys below, with clacking keys and a margin bell. It was #51 among paid Entertainment apps on the US App Store on 18 November.

item.title: Gemini 4 Neon: new model in the Gemini app for AI Pro and Ultra
item.description: Gemini 4 Neon is rolling out from 18 November in the Gemini app for AI Pro and AI Ultra subscribers, where it shows up as Deeper analysis in the model picker. It takes the place of Gemini 4 Argon, and Gemini 3.1 Pro is going away.

item.title: Gemini app now works on Android Go phones with less memory
item.description: Google has rebuilt the Gemini app so it runs on eligible Android Go edition phones, which until now only had basic voice commands. Gemini Live, camera help and image creation come with it.

item.title: GTA 6 PC download scam: fake files carry malware, NordVPN warns
item.description: There is no GTA 6 PC version, so any GTA 6 PC download is fake: NordVPN found a ready-made scam kit selling for 200 dollars that turns those downloads into malware. The game comes out on consoles on 19 November.

item.title: Instagram edit story after posting: 15 minutes to fix text and music
item.description: You can now edit an Instagram Story after posting it, changing its text, music, stickers and drawings for up to 15 minutes. Views, likes and replies stay on the Story, and an Edited label shows in the top right corner.

item.title: InviteJam: free online invitations with RSVP tracking
item.description: InviteJam is a new website for making digital invitations from more than 300 designs and tracking who's coming. Guests reply through a link without an app or an account.

item.title: iPhone Duo battery: Duodometer estimates each of the two cells
item.description: Duodometer is a $0.99 app made for the iPhone Duo's two batteries: next to the combined charge it estimates how full the main and cover cells are. It was #92 among paid Utilities apps on the US App Store on 18 November.

item.title: Kindle vs Kobo for Libby library books and EPUB files explained
item.description: The main difference between a Kindle and a Kobo is how you get books onto it: Libby library loans reach a Kindle only in the US, while Kobo has Libby built in for 13 countries and opens EPUB files directly.

item.title: McDonald's Discord order: get McDelivery through Uber Eats in chat
item.description: McDonald's added an Order McDonald's activity to Discord that lets you order McDelivery through Uber Eats in a server, channel or direct message, without leaving the chat or your game. It was announced on 18 November.

item.title: Moonlock for iPhone checks scam texts, links and QR codes
item.description: MacPaw's security app Moonlock is now on iPhone: it checks suspicious texts, screenshots, links and QR codes for signs of phishing and explains why something looks like a scam. It also tells you if your email address showed up in a data breach.

item.title: My Bookmarks app for iPhone saves links from any app, with a PIN vault
item.description: My Bookmarks is a 2.99 dollar bookmarks app for iPhone and iPad that saves links from Safari, Chrome or any app through the Share button and keeps them on your device. It was #78 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 18 November, five days after it came out.

item.title: Open Chair Finder app asks friends for you when your game needs a player
item.description: Open Chair Finder is a 2.99 dollar iPhone app that fills an empty spot in a game: you pick the activity, time and place, and it asks your friends one by one in your order, or all at once. It was #43 among paid Lifestyle apps on the US App Store on 18 November.

item.title: Powday snow forecast app gives ski areas a 15-day snowfall outlook
item.description: Powday is a free snow forecast app for skiers and snowboarders that gives every ski area worldwide a snowfall forecast for up to 15 days, blended from six or more weather models. It was #62 among free Weather apps on the US App Store on 18 November.

item.title: Qobuz Apple TV app is out, with hi-res music up to 24-bit/192 kHz
item.description: The Qobuz Apple TV app came out on 18 November in every country where Qobuz runs, for Apple TV 4th generation and later with tvOS 26 or newer. It plays the whole catalogue lossless, up to 24-bit/192 kHz.

item.title: Samsung Now Brief may get Daily Briefing with automatic reminders
item.description: Screenshots shared by SamMobile show a Daily Briefing in Now Brief that pulls bills, deadlines and appointments from your apps and turns them into reminders, Android Authority reports. Samsung hasn't confirmed it.

item.title: Senti private journal app for iPhone keeps entries on your phone
item.description: Senti is a new journal for iPhone and iPad where you type, speak or add photos, with no account, no ads and no subscription. It was #78 among paid Lifestyle apps on the US App Store on 18 November.

item.title: The Birth Bag: labor support app for birth partners, made by a doula
item.description: The Birth Bag is a new $4.99 iPhone app that guides birth partners, doulas and nurses through labor with position ideas and comfort steps. It was #31 among paid Health & Fitness apps on the US App Store on 18 November.

item.title: VWFNDR + MBL camera app now on iPhone with new color grades
item.description: The VWFNDR + MBL camera app, which launched on Android in May, is now on iPhone with version 2.0. It saves an untouched RAW (DNG) file next to each photo and adds three color grades: NATURAL, NIHON and B+W.

item.title: Wandrer iOS app is out, plus a Garmin Edge app and new routing
item.description: Wandrer, which tracks the new roads you ride, run or walk, has launched its iPhone app, which records activities and shows your new-road progress live. A Garmin Edge app and two new route planners came with it.

item.title: WhatsApp sticker reactions in testing: up to 20 stickers a message
item.description: WhatsApp is testing reactions with stickers on Android, so you can react to a message with stickers from your own collection instead of only one emoji. It's in beta 2.26.46.5 for some testers, according to WABetaInfo; WhatsApp hasn't announced it.

item.title: Apple outage on 17 November: iCloud sign-in, App Store and Apple Pay hit
item.description: Many Apple users couldn't sign in to iCloud, download apps or use Apple Music on 17 November, and some were signed out of their iPhone or Mac. Apple said an internal update caused the outage and that many systems were back up later that day.

item.title: AirTag in checked luggage: TSA rules and sharing it with your airline
item.description: An AirTag is allowed in checked and carry-on bags in the US, because its small coin battery stays inside the tracker, and since iOS 18.2 you can send its location to more than 50 airlines when a bag goes missing.

item.title: Apple Health app redesign in iOS 27.3 needs an iPhone 15 Pro or newer
item.description: The new Health app coming with iOS 27.3 in December runs on Apple Intelligence, so it only shows up on an iPhone 15 Pro or newer with Apple Intelligence turned on. Older iPhones keep the current app.

item.title: Avos News: AI news brief by email from the sources you pick
item.description: Avos reads the feeds, YouTube channels and X accounts you choose overnight and sends one email with the news at the time you set. Each story shows up once, even if several of your sources cover it.

item.title: ChatGPT GPT-6.2: new Astra and Sol models for Plus and Pro users
item.description: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol in ChatGPT and Codex on 17 November for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users. Astra is meant for hard, long projects, Sol for everyday writing and coding.

item.title: Chrome 158 update: 204 security fixes for Windows, Mac and Android
item.description: Google's Chrome 158 is rolling out to everyone with 204 security fixes, six of them rated critical, on Windows, Mac, Linux and Android. Computers get version 158.0.8127.36 or .37 over the next few days, Android gets 158.0.8127.42.

item.title: Disney Plus Hulu app merger: one app with live TV in December
item.description: Disney says Hulu's last missing parts, its live TV service and some premium add-ons, move into the Disney+ app in December, giving subscribers what it calls a fully unified experience. It announced this with its quarterly earnings on 17 November.

item.title: Dithering camera app DIITR shoots retro pixel photos and video
item.description: DIITR is a new $1.99 iPhone camera app that applies dithering, the dotted pixel look of old screens and printers, live in the viewfinder for photos and videos. It was #61 in Photo & Video on the US App Store's paid chart on 17 November.

item.title: Dreadcast weather radar app puts storms and wildfires on one map
item.description: Dreadcast is a free weather app that starts with the radar map, with layers for satellite, wind, temperature, tropical storms, wildfires, earthquakes and volcanoes. It was #100 among free Weather apps on the US App Store on 17 November.

item.title: Emulators on iPhone explained: Delta, RetroArch and what's allowed
item.description: Since April 2024 Apple has let retro game emulators like Delta and RetroArch into the App Store, but the apps come without games, and playing copies of games you download from the web is usually against copyright law.

item.title: Ethos family routine app shares chores and schedules on iPhone
item.description: Ethos is a new planner for your own weekly routine and the household's: shared routines, rotating chores and a shared shopping list, on iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple Watch. It's free to use, and Ethos Plus costs 99 cents a month, 4.99 dollars a year or 12.99 dollars once.

item.title: Final Cut Pro 13 update adds MotionVFX effects for Creator Studio
item.description: Final Cut Pro 13 now includes thousands of MotionVFX themes, transitions, titles and effects, which used to cost up to 350 dollars a year on their own. The new features are only in the Creator Studio version, not the one-time purchase.

item.title: Fubo now includes Disney+ and Hulu with ads on Pro and Elite plans
item.description: Fubo is adding the ad-supported Disney+ and Hulu bundle, a 12.99 dollar a month value, to its Pro and Elite plans from this week without raising their prices. Current subscribers get it once their eligibility is confirmed.

item.title: Gemini Tasks now free: the AI agent no longer needs AI Pro
item.description: Tasks, the Gemini app's agent that carries out jobs for you, is free from 17 November in the US, Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia and India; before, it needed an AI Pro plan. It used to be called Spark.

item.title: Google Home plays the wrong song on Spotify for some Gemini users
item.description: Owners of Nest speakers and displays say Gemini for Home often plays a different song, album or artist than the one they asked for on Spotify, and alarm routines tied to songs are hit too. Most of the reports came in on 16 and 17 November.

item.title: Google Wallet iPhone app is out in the US, without tap to pay
item.description: Google Wallet is now a free iPhone app in the US for tickets, boarding passes, loyalty cards, receipts and package tracking. You can't use it to tap and pay in shops on iOS.
